title: August 2026 fresh-intake production - batch G2 (the two asks the fifth submission established that the bank could not answer)
note: Second fresh-intake batch, authorised by the same per-occurrence adjudication record as G1. Both cards are two-occurrence cards, and neither merge was made by the parser - each is recorded in the adjudication so it can be reviewed. G2-001 answers a casualty that TWO examiners asked about in the same window: Nair asked S004 for 'a recent bulk carrier accident' (AUG-0035, held as AMBIGUOUS because no casualty was named) and Senthil asked S005 for the Ocean Winner by name (AUG-0050). S005 therefore RESOLVED a batch-3 hold, and AUG-0035 is the source because it is the earlier occurrence. G2-002 merges the leak limb (AUG-0044) into the fire limb (AUG-0042) because both are the same bunkering operation and two cards would have duplicated the whole of the ESD, coupling, water-curtain and cryogenic context. NOTE ON EXAMINER ATTRIBUTION: neither card names an examiner. Senthil is individually attributed on AUG-0050 by the candidate, but the examiner index derives from its own governed evidence ledger and writing a relationship in through card markup would bypass it - so relationships stay at 958 and the attribution is recorded in the intake store instead. NOTE ON CURRENCY: G2-001 concerns an OPEN casualty with seafarers still missing. It states the cause as undetermined and offers the liquefaction mechanism as hypothesis, never as finding.

cards.topic: MV Ocean Winner - what is established, what is not, and the liquefaction mechanism behind a Group A cargo listing and sinking in under ten minutes
LNG bunkering emergency response - leak at the manifold, and minor versus major fire, built around whether the source can be isolated
